messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), the melting/freezing point of pure water drops below 0 °C.  
According to the water phase diagram, the solid–liquid equilibrium line at 10 kPa lies at roughly **–2 °C** (≈ −1.9 °C).  

So, water would freeze at about **–2 °C** when the ambient pressure is 10 kPa.
